scope: Android renderer source investigation and one compact-navigation CSS candidate; not an established release-memory improvement

frozenSource.change: Add overflow: visible only to the Android .sidebar rule inside @media (max-width: 540px), line 494.

candidate.observedCause: The compact vertical-rail overflow-y:auto rule survives conversion into a fixed horizontal phone navigation bar. Actual WebView 156 reports the sidebar as an accelerated overflow scroller, with 178-device-pixel viewport height, 179-device-pixel painted content height, and a narrow accelerated scrollbar.
candidate.sourceCause: At ordinary scaling the Android 64 CSS px border-box bar, 8 CSS px vertical padding and 1 CSS px border leave 55 CSS px for navigation buttons with a 56 CSS px minimum height.
candidate.mechanism: Reset both overflow axes to visible for the compact horizontal Android bar, removing the accidental scroll-container requirement without clipping navigation content. This may remove a compositor scroll node, scrollbar and associated backing allocation; no resulting layer-count, byte or PSS reduction has been measured.
unchanged: All seven navigation destinations and handlers
Accessible names, titles and current-page semantics
Fonts, line heights, touch targets, labels and icons
Bar height, positioning, safe-area padding and content bottom reservation
Article frame origin and all reader functionality
candidate.risk: Visible overflow can paint content or focus outlines outside the navigation box. Android accessibility text/display enlargement and keyboard focus traversal require runtime checks; source review is not a substitute. Four reported layers do not imply four textures or that all four disappear.

allocator.warning: Allocator categories and ownership graphs overlap. Do not sum these values or equate them with PSS, retained ownership, or collectible savings.

heap.warning: Structural schema/count checks and shallow self_size aggregation only. No dominator or retained-size analysis was performed. Serialized heap nodes are not DOM nodes and these values do not account for the complete native renderer.

rejectedHypotheses: Theme classification is already lazy for Archive Original: fresh original mode does not run per-element computed-style inspection, dataset access or backdrop-cache population. The measured three native DOMStringMap objects also contradict an article-wide dataset allocation explanation for this state.

No unconditional full-article HTML/text clone cache was found. Annotation indexing is already lazy; speech and live export broad scans are command-driven. The snapshot does not establish a duplicated full article tree or a retained buffer responsible for the full deficit.

The shell root has scrollHeight 751 and clientHeight 751. Body rounding to 752 with a fractional 751.644 rect does not demonstrate a one-pixel document scroll range. No speculative height-rounding fix was made.

The prior root-overflow experiment already tested html:has(.rw-page > .rw-archive-frame){overflow:hidden!important} under zero root scroll range and did not establish a useful gain. It was not repeated.

The earlier opaque experiment changed the iframe element background only. Actual archive body is already opaque rgb(248,249,250), while html is transparent. No evidence establishes missing child-canvas opacity; no root-color alteration was made, preserving Archive Original appearance.
The mobile rw-statusbar is intentional floating reader controls/status, not an obsolete hidden footer. It was preserved.
Additional .apk resident mappings and Intl/ICU startup are leads, not proven sources of removable memory. No localization functionality was removed or replaced.
